info.name: EnTur API — Ruter Debug
info.description:
Tests for EnTur JourneyPlanner v3 GraphQL + Pelias geocoder.
Import this into Postman to verify departures, trip planner, and stop search.

Base URL: https://api.entur.io
No API key needed — just set ET-Client-Name header.

request.description:
Search for Visperud stop.
Expect: features[].properties.id starting with NSR:StopPlace:
If sources=nsr is removed, you'll get addresses and POIs with non-NSR IDs.

Search for Sinsenveien.
Look at features[].properties.id — note ALL returned IDs.
There may be multiple stops (one per direction/quay group).
This helps identify which NSR:StopPlace ID is the correct one for your commute.

Without sources=nsr you get addresses, street segments, and POIs.
These IDs cannot be used in stopPlace() queries — they fail silently.

Uses serviceJourney → journeyPattern → line (the correct OTP2 path).

Check:
- Does it return HTTP 200?
- Is json.errors empty?
- Is stopPlace.estimatedCalls an array with data?
- Does each call have serviceJourney.journeyPattern.line.publicCode populated?

If journeyPattern is null on all calls → the schema path is wrong on this server.

item.name: Departures: Visperud (direct line path — old, may fail)

request.description:
Uses serviceJourney → line directly (the OLD path that may not exist in OTP2).

If this returns json.errors → the field doesn't exist and we need journeyPattern.
If BOTH work → either path is fine and the bug is elsewhere.

Departures from Sinsenveien (NSR:StopPlace:58221).

Check quay.name and quay.description — this tells you which direction each departure is going.
If you see departures going BOTH directions from the same stop, then the stop ID covers both quays.

item.name: Departures: Introspect quays at a stop

request.description:
Lists all quays (platforms) at the stop with their IDs, names, and compass bearing.
compassBearing tells you the physical direction buses travel from that quay.
This helps understand if the stop covers both directions or just one.

Trip from Sinsenveien to Visperud (the Home preset).

Check:
- How many tripPatterns are returned?
- Do ALL legs use bus 100? If yes, that IS the only transit link.
- What are the leg modes? (foot, bus, metro, etc.)
- Does expectedStartTime differ across patterns?

If you only see bus 100: the stop IDs might be correct but your commute goes through bus 100.
If you see errors in json.errors: the query schema is wrong.
Trip from Visperud to Sinsenveien (the Work preset).

item.name: Trip: Visperud → Oslo S (broad city center test)

request.description:
Trip from Visperud to Oslo S (NSR:StopPlace:59872 = Oslo Sentralstasjon).
Useful to see if different lines appear when the destination is a known major hub.
If this shows multiple different lines → the preset stop IDs might be too close together.

item.name: Trip: Schema introspect — check field names

request.description:
Introspects the TripPattern type to list all available fields.
Verify: are expectedStartTime / expectedEndTime the real field names?
OTP2 sometimes uses aimedStartTime instead.

Introspects the Leg type.
Verify: is 'line' a direct field on Leg, or only via serviceJourney?
This is the key question for whether serviceJourney.journeyPattern.line or leg.line is correct.

Lists all fields on ServiceJourney.
Key check: does ServiceJourney have a 'line' field directly?
Or is it only accessible via journeyPattern?
This directly answers the departure query schema question.

Lists all fields on EstimatedCall (the object inside estimatedCalls[]).
Useful to find if there are better fields for line/direction info.
